perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information:

- He is a police officer and has been close childhood friends with Jonathan. He often seeks Jonathan’s advice on personal and professional matters and values Jonathan’s perspective.
- He has noticed Jonathan acting differently and believes Jonathan is hiding something important. This makes him anxious and suspicious.
- He arranges a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop and confronts him about hiding something.
- He hears Jonathan admit that he has been keeping something from Christian and that he is in some trouble.
- Christian offers to help and says they can face it together. Jonathan tells him the situation is complicated and he did not want to drag Christian into it, but he could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian asks whether the trouble is related to anything illegal. Jonathan says he cannot say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but that he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian decides to look into the matter discreetly to make sure Jonathan is safe. Jonathan thanks him and says he trusts Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian comes to believe/report that Jonathan is being framed and that someone is trying to set him up. He tells Jonathan this, says he has leads but not the full answer yet, and decides to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Later, Christian identifies/reports that the person behind it is someone both he and Jonathan know and trust. He feels betrayed and resolute and decides to confront that person and bring them to justice.
- He hears Jonathan warn him that this person is dangerous, but Jonathan says he trusts Christian to do what is right.

Christian does not have direct access to hidden events or private information beyond what he observed, was told, or discovered through his own investigation.
